messages:
Sam: Quick check — we're iterating on the proxy routing plugin that decides region + fallback. current behavior pins to primary region, then switches to global fallback during overload. thinking about tightening the interface so routing decisions can encode 'privacy-zone' hints (eu-only, can-fallback-to-us, no-fallback). Any objections?
Maria: I like explicit hints. Right now the plugin surface is tiny: route(ctx) -> region. We should instead return (region, policy) so the caller can apply consistent SLO/telemetry.
Kevin: Important: policy needs to capture KV residency constraints. If a tenant is eu-only, we must never fall back to a non-eu region even under surge. That's a hard constraint, not an advisory.
Anya: Agreed. Also remember KMS scope — keys are region-scoped for on-prem customers. If routing moves request to a different region we also need to assert crypto eligibility.
Sam: Proposal sketch: RouteDecision {region: "eu-west-1", fallbackMode: "none", residencyTag: "eu", auditTags:["PII:high"]}. Example: {region: "eu-west-1", fallbackMode: "none", residencyTag: "eu", auditTags:["PII:high"]}
Maria: That works. Two tradeoffs: 1) adds complexity to proxies that have to interpret fallbackMode and residencyTag; 2) forces callers to implement consistent degrade flows (e.g., lower request size / model quality). But it centralizes policy in route selection which we want.
Kevin: Can we keep a simple default path where older proxies get a scalar 'preferred_region' and newer ones use the richer object? Backwards compatibility matters.
Sam: Yes — router will continue to return simple string for v1 clients, but v2 clients can opt-in via Accept-Routing: v2 header. We'll maintain a graceful fallback.
Anya: Rollout checklist: - API contract in proxy repo - unit tests for residency invariant - KMS check in key-manager service - telemetry (route_decision.*, fallback_triggered) - canary in dedicated eu-only tenants
Maria: On the degrade strategy, i'd rather 'degrade-local' mean: try sibling racks in same region first, then warm standby in region with same residency if available; 'degrade-global' is the last resort but only for residencyTag==any. Documented in the interface.
Sam: +1. Also add a small code example for engineers:
```
// pseudocode in proxy-plugin
decision = router.route(ctx)
if decision.fallbackMode == 'none': enforceLocalOnly()
elif decision.fallbackMode == 'degrade-local': attemptLocalFallbackSequence()
else: globalFallbackWithRateLimit()
```
Kevin: Metrics to add: route_decision.residency, route_decision.fallback_mode, fallback.latency_impact, fallback.token_cost_delta. Ops wants alert when fallback_rate > 0.5% for eu-only tenants.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: refactor-routing-interface @sam (PR #6423) — staging rollout started :construction: https://git.internal/r/6423
Sam: I'll own the PR review and the canary for eu-only test tenants tomorrow. If no blockers, we merge and roll to staging this week.
Maria: I'll update docs and add the degrade definitions to the developer guide.
Anya: I'll add KMS gating test and a TDD for on-prem key scope.
Kevin: Great. Action items captured. 👍
